neighbours.label: do / don't handling instructions in health-hazard precautions (raw meat and germs, lead, asbestos, plastics in the microwave, fumes); the same instruction frames about harmless things are quieter
fire: Scrub the cutting board with hot soapy water after it touches raw poultry.
Never try to remove old lead paint yourself with a heat gun.
Do not heat baby formula in plastic bottles in the microwave.
Wash your hands thoroughly after cleaning up mouse droppings.
If the insulation may contain asbestos, do not disturb it yourself.
Keep raw eggs away from salads, and wash the bowl before you reuse it.
Never use a charcoal grill inside a tent or a garage.
Rinse your eyes with clean water if pesticide splashes into them, and do not rub.
quiet: Scrub the patio with a stiff broom before you paint the fence.
Never try to tune an old piano yourself without a proper lever.
Do not leave baby photos in plastic sleeves in the attic.
Fold your shirts neatly after sorting the laundry.
If the invitation may contain a typo, do not print it yet.
Keep spare keys away from the door, and label the hook before you forget.
Never use a red pen on a form or a cheque.
Trim your hedge with sharp shears if branches grow into the path, and do not rush.

notes: Weak pole (max 5.7); the - pole fires on the toxic agents themselves (fluoride, lead, radiation). Probes: hazard advice 0.07-0.47 (median about 0.2), harmless instructions 0.02-0.20. Expect a marginal result.
